claims.text: The starting FeCoNi alloy is homogeneous and single-phase fcc.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
The baseline coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi is approximately 100 Oe or less.
Solution treatment near 1100°C followed by aging near 500°C for about 1 hour and rapid quenching can produce the proposed microstructure.
The aging treatment will induce nanoscale L1₀-ordered CoFe precipitates in the fcc FeCoNi matrix.
The aging parameters can be tuned to make the L1₀ precipitates moderately or slightly incoherent with the fcc matrix.
Moderately incoherent L1₀ precipitates generate localized strain fields.
The precipitates and their localized strain fields act as domain-wall-pinning sites.
Pinning by the precipitates impedes domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion will increase the coercive field.
The aging treatment will raise the coercive field significantly above 100 Oe.
The treated alloy may reach a coercive field of 200–300 Oe.
The coercivity increase can be achieved without notably reducing saturation magnetization.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or complete phase separation must be avoided to obtain the intended magnetic response.
The proposed outcome is limited to near-equiatomic FeCoNi alloys that retain a dominant fcc matrix.

contradictions.description: The predicted range begins at 200 Oe while the baseline may be 100 Oe, yielding an increase of exactly 100 Oe, but the example falsification threshold requires an increase greater than 100 Oe. Thus part of the predicted range would not satisfy the stated success criterion.
